newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Former Vietnam war foes eye military cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Former Vietnam war foes eye military cooperation.

text.p: U.S. Admiral Joseph Prueher said on Friday Washington wanted to build on a nascent military relationship with Vietnam through personnel exchanges or tactical discussions.

Prueher, commander-in-chief for the Pacific, told journalists at a news briefing in Hanoi he had discussed with Vietnamese officials plans for a meeting later this year to explore avenues for bilateral cooperation.

"I'll reiterate it's a nascent military relationship, and without an endgame in sight," he said. "But what we're talking about doing is getting a colonel-level group...I propose to have that meet in Hanoi next summer."
Prueher added that he had also talked about military and diplomatic visits by Vietnamese officials to an Asia-Pacific centre for strategic studies in Honolulu.

He said the two sides might also look at exchanges involving military training, including jungle warfare training, adding that Hanoi had expressed strong support for a continued U.S. military presence in the region.
Prueher is the most senior U.S. military official to visit Vietnam since Washington normalised diplomatic relations with Hanoi in 1995, 20 years after the end of the Vietnam war.
In recent years the former adversaries have been working together to resolve the fate of the 2,128 U.S. servicemen who are still listed as missing in action in Indochina.
Prueher said the Vietnamese government was cooperating in full over the issue but added, without explanation, that this did not mean Hanoi could not do better.
Prueher's visit to Vietnam comes during a dispute between Hanoi and Beijing over oil exploration in contested waters in the South China Sea.
Vietnam announced last weekend it had protested to China over the positioning of a rig some 64.5 nautical miles off its central coast.
Prueher said the United States was optimistic that the two nations would resolve the matter peacefully.
The U.S. admiral held talks with Vietnam's Defence Minister earlier in the day and had been scheduled to meet Vietnam's Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet later on Friday.
However he indicated delays in Kiet's agenda meant the meeting might now not take place.
